text:
Feifer c. Feldman

2024 QCCS 643

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUEBEC

DISTRICT OF

Montreal

No:

500-17-112885-200

DATE:

February 8, 2024

_____________________________________________________________________

PRESIDING

THE HONOURABLE

THOMAS M. DAVIS, J.S.C.

_____________________________________________________________________

Dr. ANDREW FEIFER

-and-

JONATHAN JACOB FEIFER

Plaintiffs

v.

GLENN
J. FELDMAN

Defendant

_____________________________________________________________________

JUDGMENT

_____________________________________________________________________

OVERVIEW

[
1
]

Drawn into what is essentially an acrimonious
dispute between two former business partners, Plaintiffs Andrew Feifer
(Andrew)

and Jonathan-Jacob Feifer
(Jonathan),
personally and in their capacity
as liquidators of the estate of their late mother, Sherry Lande Feifer
(Sherry)
,
seek a permanent injunction to prevent Defendant G. Joseph Feldman
(Feldman)
[1]
from publishing,
disseminating, broadcasting or otherwise communicating certain information that
he claims to possess. He posits that Sherry benefited from gold bars made up of
gold illegally stolen by the Nazis from Jewish people living in Germany during
the Nazi regime.

[
2
]

The gold bars, or the proceeds thereof, would
have been inherited from her mother Mia Lande
(Mia)
, via the estate of Sherry’s
father, Martin Lande
(Martin)
, who himself would have either inherited
or misappropriated the bars from Dr. Ludwig Delphiner who immigrated to Canada
in 1926. Dr. Delphiner is alleged to have been a Nazi officer who participated
in the thefts and removed the gold bars to Canada.

[
3
]

The brothers and Sherry’s estate also seek
$1,500,000 in punitive damages and $350,000 in extrajudicial fees. The brothers
ask the Court for $500,000 each in moral damages.

[
4
]

Surprisingly, Feldman made a cross application in
the amount of $3.75 million. He desisted from same at trial, but the totally
unfounded nature of his cross application will be part of the discussion of
Plaintiffs’ claim for extrajudicial fees.

1.

CONTEXT

1.1

The Parties

1.1.1

The Feifer family

[
5
]

To fully comprehend the feelings of Plaintiffs
when they became aware of Feldman’s allegations, it is important for the Court
to briefly relate the values of the Feifer family.

[
6
]

Andrew and Jonathan are fully aware of the
extremely difficult childhood of their maternal grandparents, Martin and Mia,
their survival of the horrors of the Holocaust and their immigration to Canada,
after living in Israel for a short time. Andrew relates it in his testimony.
The Court also had the benefit of a video of Mia relating some of the family’s
history
[2]

when she was interviewed in 1997 for the Shoah Visual History project.

[
7
]

Feldman objected to the production of the video
on the basis of relevance. The Court will discuss the objection below.

[
8
]

Martin and Mia lost many family members in the
Holocaust, including their fathers. They survived concentration and death camps
and immigrated to Canada after the war in 1950-51; they were among the few
survivors in the family.

[
9
]

Following their arrival in Canada, Martin and
Mia worked very hard to establish their business and to provide for their
family. The grandparents were proud of their Jewish faith and heritage. They believed
that it was important for the entire family to understand and embrace the Jewish
faith and passed their values down to their daughter Sherry and ultimately to
Andrew and Jonathan.

[
10
]

Growing-up, Plaintiffs’ home was one where the
Jewish faith was both important and practiced. Their father, Gerald, was Vice-president
of the family’s synagogue, and the family attended services every Saturday. A
video taken in Gerald’s hospital room shortly before his death during Hannukah
in 2015, shows the extent of the family’s devotion to Jewish tradition.
[3]
Understanding the Holocaust
was front and center in that devotion, especially given the experience of the
maternal grandparents.

[
11
]

Plaintiffs attended Jewish schools in Montreal
as well as Jewish summer camp. They participated in many Jewish organisations
and activities such as CJA and the March of the Living. In 2024, Andrew’s son
will be part of the 30
th
anniversary March of the Living and Andrew
will be a monitor. Jonathan’s children are younger, but are attending Jewish
schools in New York, where he lives.

[
12
]

Andrew is a urologist specializing in urologic
oncology surgery. There is an important research component to his practice, and
he has received numerous research grants. He is a faculty member in the Faculty
of Medicine at both the University of Toronto and McMaster University.
[4]
He resides in Toronto with his
family, and they live in the respect of traditional Jewish values that were
part of Andrew’s life growing up.

[
13
]

Jonathan is the managing partner of Park Stone
Management LLC, an investment company that owns, operates, and develops real
estate assets in mass transit anchored communities. He founded the company in
2013. The nature of the business makes relationships with investors and
partners in projects very important. Living in New York, Jonathan deals with
many professionals of the Jewish faith. Reputation is important in his
business.

[
14
]

In addition, Jonathan manages a portfolio of
stabilized multifamily assets in the greater New York area.

[
15
]

The brothers continue to have a significant
attachment to Montreal and Quebec. They return often and are members of a prominent
synagogue here as well as one in Sainte-Agathe-des-Monts, where they share a
country home.

[
16
]

On their mother’s passing they inherited her
estate, which included one half of Mia’s estate. The settlement of Sherry’s
estate apparently took around eight years, with the distributions having been
completed around a year and a half ago. Andrew and Irwin Lande
(Lande)
,
Sherry’s brother, were co-liquidators.

1.1.2

Irwin Lande

[
17
]

Lande is a Montreal businessman, working
primarily in the real estate industry for over 35 years. The evidence shows
that there was a degree of acrimony between him and his sister. Andrew and
Jonathan were not immune to the acrimony, as Lande was displeased with some of
the bequests of jewelry and trinkets in Mia’s will.

[
18
]

For much of his 35 years in the real estate
industry he and Feldman were partners and still own several properties together.
Unfortunately, there is also seemingly uncontrolled acrimony between these
former close friends that, in many ways, is at the root of the present dispute.

[
19
]

After becoming aware of the inheritance received
by Lande from Mia’s estate, or perhaps when Lande began to spend large sums of
money to renovate his home, Feldman’s behavior toward his friend changed, the
details of which the Court will discuss below. Feldman began to make allegations
about Lande, some of which are related in a distinct lawsuit instituted by
Lande on March 23, 2020
(the Commercial Proceedings)
to dissolve their
partnership in an immovable that they held jointly with other partners,
including Sherry’s estate.
[5]

1.1.3

Dr. Ludwig Delphiner

[
20
]

Dr. Ludwig Delphiner was a scientist who Feldman
believes was part of an alleged theft of gold from Holocaust victims
(the
Nazi gold)
. Dr. Delphiner would have participated in the theft of the gold and
held it in the form of gold bars at his home in Île Bizard. As the Court has said,
the gold bars would have eventually ended up in the patrimony of Martin and
Mia, to be ultimately bequeathed to Lande and Sherry by Mia. Andrew and
Jonathan would have received their mother’s share of this illicit asset.

[
21
]

Plaintiffs retort that Dr. Delphiner was not an
officer with Adolf Hitler’s German Third Reich regime, but rather lead by
example throughout his life as a decorated soldier in the Austrian Cavalry in
the First World War, chief chemist (as of 1930) and production manager at
Abbott Laboratories in Montreal and later, as a member of its Board of
Directors from 1947. He was also a Fellow of the Chemical Institute of Canada.

[
22
]

Dr. Delphiner was the cousin of Plaintiffs’ great-grandmother
but was also referred to as “uncle” or “great-uncle.” While he was generally
known as Ludwig, he was called Littman as well.

[
23
]

Andrew and Jonathan were both young when he
passed and have no personal knowledge of his will, the bequests therein, or the
value of his estate.

[
24
]

Some evidence demonstrates that in 2004, Andrew
and Jonathan’s father, Gerald, may have consulted the probate file of Dr.
Delphiner’s will, but they cannot say why. His name is written on a copy of the
plumitif of the file.
[6]

1.2

Feldman’s Affirmations

[
25
]

Feldman is a lawyer and member of the Quebec Bar
since 1981. He is also a businessman working primarily in the real estate
industry.

[
26
]

Because of his friendship with Lande, apparently
since the two were in high school, he was often in Martin and Mia’s home and
has known Andrew and Jonathan since their childhood. He enjoyed a closer relationship
with Jonathan.

[
27
]

Because Sherry’s estate was a shareholder in the
property that was the subject of the Commercial Proceedings
(the
Sainte-Catherine Street Property)
, Feldman had business dealings with
Plaintiffs. Given the friction between Sherry and Lande, and the later tension
over the bequests of Mia’s jewelry, Feldman asserts that there was little
dialogue between Sherry and her brother and that, as such, he often discussed
the building with Jonathan.

[
28
]

As the Court has said, Feldman’s falling-out
with Lande seems to have begun with his suspicions over the money that his
partner was spending to renovate his residence in an expensive and opulent
manner.
[7]

Feldman believed that the money that Lande was paying to contractors went well
beyond the income that could be generated from the partners’ business ventures.

[
29
]

What is more, an audit of the business showed
all to be in order. So, where did the money come from?

[
30
]

Feldman states that the other partners in some
of his and Lande’s real estate ventures, particularly the one that is the
subject of the Commercial Proceedings, were asking questions.

[
31
]

An apparent special resolution,
relating to that immovable, was signed by some of the special partners and
general partners of Société en Commandite Montreal Media et Divertissement, on
March 11, 2020.
[8]

The allegations were far reaching:

We have been made acutely aware of
Mr. Feldman's claim and supportive evidence which allege that your funds, as
well as those of your father, Martin Lande and mother, Mia Lande were illegally
misappropriated from Dr. Ludwig Littman Delphiner's Estate and that the origin
thereof may have been related to economic crimes against the Jewish Holocaust
and Victims Concentration Camps in Auschwitz.

[…]

This Resolution will apply equally
to any units held by Jonathan Jacob Feifer and/or Andrew Feifer. We understand
that the units were to be traded according to Mr. Irwin Lande's statements to
Mrs. Carola Reda on March 9, 2020. No trade will be permitted for the time
being in respect to Mr. Irwin Lande's units or shares held by himself and/or by
the Estate of the Late Mia Lande.

[
32
]

This resolution led Lande to institute the
Commercial Proceedings which were initially managed by Justice Paquette, as she
then was.

[
33
]

But why involve Plaintiffs? As the Court has
said, Sherry’s estate held part of the building and, according to Feldman, if
Lande was benefiting from the proceeds of Nazi gold, so were they. Feldman
continued to involve them into the dispute. He could not bear the fact that
they were supporting Lande in his bid to have the partnership in the building
liquidated, according to Feldman at great loss to him and some of the other
partners.

[
34
]

Further documents produced or exchanged during
the proceedings accused Andrew and Jonathan of teaming up with their uncle to
protect their own fortunes.
[9]

[
35
]

Curiously, following Justice Paquette’s judgment
appointing an interim receiver, Feldman drafted and deposited a “Long-Form
Affidavit” directly at her office, but not into the Court file. It contained serious
affirmations about Nazi gold stolen from Holocaust victims by Dr. Delphiner in
Poland, which gold would have been left to Martin, such that Lande and
Plaintiffs became the benefactors
(the Long Form Affidavit)
.
[10]
Given that there will be a
sealing order in respect of the Long Form Affidavit, the Court will not provide
a complete recital of the allegations, as they could no doubt harm Andrew and
Jonathan’s reputations if additional elements of them were to find their way
into the public domain. In the Court’s words, here are some of the allegations:

•

Feldman’s story begins at the time of the
probate of Dr. Delphiner’s will in 1983. He alleges having been with Lande and
Martin to conduct an estate inventory of the home of Dr. Delphiner. “While
conducting an inventory of the assets I discovered a concrete encased room
measuring approximately 12'x 9' in the basement (lower level) in which I
observed 8 palettes of stacked metal bars.” He now assumes that they were gold.

•

He believes that Dr. Delphiner was a Waffen S.S.
officer, with Adolf Hitler's German Third Reich regime at the Auschwitz death
camps in Nazi occupied Poland during the Second World War, which gave him
access to this gold.

•

Feldman went as far as to visit Dr. Delphiner’s
former home with a real estate agent on the evening of January 7, 2020. He
affirms having seen a one-pour concrete German-fashioned bunker which measured
exactly 9' by 12', equipped with a concealed steel-reinforced panic door,
battery remote lock button, surrounded by 3 to 4 feet thick cement walls with
no ventilation.

•

Assuming that the Nazi gold had been stored
there, Feldman informed some of his partners in the building that is the object
of the Commercial Proceedings, and in March convened an informal emergency
meeting to pass the special resolution, excluding Lande and Plaintiffs.

•

For Feldman, the only reason Andrew and Jonathan
took the side of Lande was to defend and protect their own inheritances.

[
36
]

Feldman’s animus towards Andrew and Jonathan
becomes more evident when he discusses the Sainte-Catherine Street Property,
perhaps the jewel in the partners’ portfolio for almost 40 years. The
receivership imposed by Justice Paquette cost the partners over $1.2 million in
fees to MNP according to Feldman and he was not happy that Lande forced it.
Lande was trying to destroy him. The nephews were assisting in Lande’s venture
by siding with their uncle.

[
37
]

Andrew and Jonathan strongly deny the
allegations of the Long Form Affidavit and refuted them in their testimony.

[
38
]

In his testimony Feldman’s acknowledges that his
first knowledge of Dr. Delphiner was in 1983, when he visited his former home
on Île Bizard with Lande. He was told that the bars he saw were scrap metal and
offered to have a jobber that he knew remove them. The offer was quickly
refused.

[
39
]

Dr. Delphiner appears to have been forgotten
about by Feldman until 2019, when he questioned Lande about the money that the
latter was spending on his home. Feldman, joking he says, asked Lande if it
might have been gold that he saw in Uncle Ludwig’s bunker. Lande’s response of
“None of your f—-ing business” surprised him as the partners had never had any
secrets from each other.

[
40
]

A few weeks later Feldman was arrested at his
home for the harassment of his partner, Lande.

[
41
]

Feldman pursued his investigation into the Nazi
gold by obtaining the plans for Lande’s home, which, according to Feldman, has
three bunkers and 120 surveillance cameras, although the plans were not
produced.

[
42
]

He then turned his attention to Dr. Delphiner’s
will. He had arranged the probate in 1983, as a lawyer for Martin. Feldman went
as far as contesting the validity of the will before this Court in proceedings
instituted in November 2020. He was not successful, but it is important to
pause and consider the judgment of Justice Philipps.

[
43
]

Justice Philipps reports that Feldman had been
one of the witnesses of the English form will, although he denied meeting the
deceased. That said, he held that Feldman lacked sufficient interest to contest
the validity of the will. However, Justice Philipps went further and found
Feldman’s action to be abusive:

[34]

On the issue of sufficient
interest, plaintiff, in oral argument, attempted to turn the tables on Mr.
Lande, claiming that it is he, Lande, who lacks proper standing to challenge
his action against his father’s estate. He referred to the fact that Mr. Irwin
Lande actually had little if anything to do with his father’s estate — which,
it should be recalled, is now the only defendant in the present proceedings —,
stressing that the late Martin Lande apparently bequeathed his estate
essentially to his wife Mia. But when pressed as to why, despite that, he nevertheless
saw fit to name Irwin Lande as
mis en cause
in these
proceedings, plaintiff made certain revealing statements about his true
intentions and the nature of his claim. Ultimately, plaintiff’s target in the
proceedings is Irwin Lande, whom he hopes to see come to ruin on the basis of
the alleged misappropriation by his father of Delphiner’s supposed riches,
which included Nazi gold taken from unsuspecting Jewish victims during the
Second World War. Or so plaintiff claims.

[35]

Although intention is not a
requirement, its presence certainly enhances the potential for legally
characterizing a set of proceedings as abusive.

[36]

The tale plaintiff tells is
quintessentially abusive. Indeed, it bears certain of the hallmarks of
vexatious litigation. It consists of an incongruous and convoluted story
of concealment, falsified genealogies, Delphiner spelled with “ph” versus
Delfiner with an “f”, communications with other Delphiners in Boston and
Philadelphia, Delphiner’s first name as having actually been Littman, the real
Ludwig Delphiner having died in 1941, the status of Martin Lande as mere friend
and not cousin, Delphiner’s work as a chemist and his knowledge and use of
sodium pentothal, Delphiner’s use of notary Robert Burke as opposed to his
usual notary Dugas and finally, gold in a bunker in a house on Île Bizard. At
the end of the day, plaintiff asserted in oral argument: “there is a story that
is somehow related to a heist of an enormous amount of gold.” Eight billion
dollars’ worth of gold. Nazi gold.
[11]

[
44
]

Feldman also places great stock into the fact
that Dr. Delphiner was cremated, apparently with no Jewish funeral and that he
was buried in a mass internment section of Mount Royal Cemetery. Justice
Philipps was even obliged to annul subpoenas that Feldman had issued to
cemetery officials and funeral directors.

[
45
]

In the pursuit of his investigation Feldman went
as far as hiring a student to do research into Dr. Delphiner. He appears to
have drawn some conclusions about Dr. Delphiner from her research, which are
not supported by it.

[
46
]

Canadian disembarkation records for Halifax on January
26, 1926, show one Littman Delfiner, born in Kolomyja, Poland, disembarking
from a ship that had sailed from Danzig on January 12. It shows the profession
as chemist and the ultimate destination as Montreal via the C.N.R.
[12]
No similar records were
produced to show how Dr. Delphiner would have returned to Europe to become an
SS officer during the Second World War, or to document a return to Canada
thereafter.

[
47
]

The Delfiner who disembarked in 1926 became a
naturalized Canadian on March 30, 1932
[13]

and, at some point, changed the spelling of his name to Delphiner.

[
48
]

The student also consulted genealogy web sites
looking for information about Dr. Delphiner. It is difficult to ascertain the
probative value of these sites, as they contain contradictory information as to
the place of birth and even the residence of the subject. It seems that some of
what is written on the sites, particularly Ancestry.com, could be somewhat subjective,
[14]
as much of the information was
entered by one Ethan Frankel, apparently a distant relative of Dr. Delphiner. The
apparent inconsistencies led Feldman to believe that the information was being
manipulated by Andrew and Jonathan following his accusations of 2019.

[
49
]

Jonathan provided context for his consultation
of various web sites on the genealogy of the Delphiner family. He wanted to
understand Dr. Delphiner better, so that he might be able to dissuade Feldman
from his assertation that Dr. Delphiner was a Nazi. He agrees that in November
2019, he spoke to Feldman at some length about the situation. He suggested to
Feldman that he resolve his issues with Lande or split the business up. Feldman
did not want to do this.

[
50
]

Plaintiffs also provided some information about
Dr. Delphiner, including the Abbott “Time, Man of the Year” edition for August
27, 1964. It would appear to contradict Feldman’s affirmation that Dr. Delfiner
was part of the Waffen SS. One extract reads:

When the firm moved to a new location
in 1940, Dr. Delphiner was responsible for setting up a large share of the
manufacturing' facilities.
[15]

[
51
]

Nothing in the evidence can explain how Dr.
Delphiner could be both in charge of setting up Abbott’s manufacturing
facilities and an officer in the SS at the same time.

[
52
]

Tellingly, Feldman acknowledged in Court that he
has no proof that Plaintiffs ultimately benefited from looted Nazi gold. His
research caused him to assume that this is the case. He admitted that he has no
direct evidence.

[
53
]

Feldman took his concerns about the Nazi gold to
many people, including Joel King of the CJA, who in turn suggested that he
contact the Lawfare Project where he spoke to Ziporah Reich. She suggested that
he contact the Honourable Irwin Cotler and the two eventually met. Feldman
maintains that Mr. Cotler asked for and was given his documentation but chose not
to get involved due to his relationship with the Feifer family. These are but
some of the people that he shared his story with.

[
54
]

Other than Mr. Cotler, there is no evidence that
either Andrew or Jonathan were known to the people or organizations that
Feldman shared his story with.

[
55
]

As mentioned, Jonathan was first brought into
the fray in November 2019, when Feldman called him to complain about his
business partner, Lande. The former also raised his suspicions about Dr.
Delphiner and the looted gold bars, but Jonathan did not take it seriously as
it seemed so far fetched. He refused to tell Feldman what he had inherited from
his mother.

[
56
]

Andrew and Jonathan soon became aware of the special
resolution of March 11, 2020, the basis of which was curiously believed by the
other shareholders who signed it, some of whom were influential and
sophisticated people in the Montreal Jewish community. Then there was a text
message to Jonathan on March 27, 2020, where Feldman said that his
investigators believed that Lande had $2.6 billion in gold from Dr. Delphiner
and strongly suggested that Plaintiffs should support the special resolution,
in return for the release of a cash distribution.
[16]

[
57
]

The Long Form Affidavit was perhaps the straw
that broke the camel’s back. Andrew and Jonathan were both horrified and
frightened by it. While Jonathan acknowledged that the allegations were very
far-fetched, Plaintiffs note that there is always a risk that some people will
believe the allegations, or at least some of them. They wanted to put a stop to
Feldman’s crusade.

[
58
]

Plaintiffs’ initial goal was for Feldman to
cease and desist. He was served a demand letter to this effect dated April 8,
2020. It had little effect. In fact, on June 5, 2020 Feldman continued his
narrative in a letter to one of Plaintiffs’ lawyers, where the allegations were
repeated and more specifically he alleged that the payment of the lawyer’s fees
was likely being done with proceeds of Dr. Delphiner’s illegally forged will.
[17]

[
59
]

Extracts from Feldman’s pre-trial examination
also demonstrate how invested he was in the litigation, all to the detriment of
Plaintiffs (and likely himself):

And he wanted to then show it to his
nephews, “You see, I’m running the whole show like... I’m king of the castle.”
But that’s not going to happen. Not going to happen. He’s not going to be kind
of the castle anymore, and neither will you guys.

Q- Me...

A. Trust me. I don’t give up. Banon
knows this. He knows I don’t give up. Right, David, you know I don’t give up. I
don’t give up.

Q- Me Feldman, if you are finished,
I...[…]A- I’m going all the way with these guys.

A- I’m just telling you, I’m going
all the way with these guys because they decided to jump into... onto Irwin’s
bandwagon. Had... if they would have done the right thing morally and towards
their Jewish community, maybe we wouldn’t be talking about this today. Not a
single... not a single document in my procedures refers to the Feifers being
complicit in this crime.[…]A- ... it’s hard to even believe that they would
have sued me, unless Irwin asked them to sue me, so that you can keep me busy
while I can’t practise law, get to my office, just keep me busy. But I’m going
to keep them busy very soon. They’re going to be busy coming to Montreal in
January, when it’s thirty below zero…
[18]

1.3

The Desfossés Judgment

[
60
]

Plaintiffs were successful in obtaining an
interlocutory injunction on June 14, 2021, in a judgment rendered by Justice
Desfossés. She notes certain judicial admissions of Feldman:

[39] The Defense also contains a
number of judicial admissions.

[40] More specifically, at
paragraph 22 of his Defense, Mr. Feldman admits the allegations contained in
paragraphs 5, 7, 8, 14, 15, 16, 21, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 32, 36, 38,
39, 51, 55, 56, 67, 69 and 76 of the Demand.

[
61
]

The admission of paragraphs 38 and 39 in the
Originating Application gives pause. They read:

38. Feldman's fictitious and
grossly defamatory statements demonstrate that there are no limits to his
pursuit of creating a fictitious narrative to accommodate his position,
particularly so as the Plaintiffs and Sherry are in fact the descendants of
Holocaust survivors, with many family members having perished in concentration
camps;

39. This obvious conclusion is
further evidenced by the astonishing inconsistencies between the Affidavit and
Feldman's sworn declaration of March 27, 2020 filed in the Commercial
Proceedings, communicated in support hereof as EXHIBIT P-12;

[
62
]

They were not formally disavowed. Mr. Feldman
believes that a young lawyer in his office made a mistake.

1.4

Developments During Case Management

[
63
]

The Long Form Affidavit was apparently returned
to Feldman by Justice Paquette, but there is another document to which the
Court must give some attention. After the undersigned was assigned to manage
the proceedings, Feldman attempted to produce what he refers to as a personal
journal. The Court refused the production in a judgment dated September 20,
2022. However, during that hearing, it appeared that Feldman had communicated
that journal to third parties and he was asked to provide a solemn declaration
conforming who had received it.

[
64
]

That declaration confirms that it was
communicated to the following people:

• Irwin Cotler – Human Rights
leader and former Attorney-General of Canada

• Ziporah Reich – Lawyer at the
Lawfare Project in New York, US

• Wesley Fischer – Member of the
Holocaust Claims Conference

• Gabriel Groisman – Mayor of Bal
Harbor, Florida, US

• Oded Zucker – Rothchild
Foundation

• Reevin Pearl – Lawyer at Pearl
and Associates

• Dan Haezrachy – World Jewish
Restitution Organization

• Alexandra Sarah Feldman – My
daughter

• Miguel Eduardo Vargas Monroy – My
lawyer – Lawyer at Feldman Avocats Inc.

• Briana Di Iorio – Paralegal at
Feldman Avocats Inc.

[
65
]

Following a further intervention of the Court,
Feldman confirmed that the said document had been provided to these people on
March 22, 2022.

[
66
]

However, other documents had been communicated
previously. In an email communicated on April 8, 2021, Feldman’s then lawyer
stated:

Regarding U-3 and U-11, Mr. Feldman
declares having sent summaries or affidavits to the following people, to the
best of his recollection:

1)

Simon Wiesenthal;

2)

the CRA;

3)

the MRQ;

4)

the IRS;

5)

the Lawfare Project;

6)

the DOJ;

7)

the IRS;

8)

Elie Wiesel;

9)

the Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs;

10)

the US Holocaust Victims council;

[19]

1.5

Media Coverage

[
67
]

The record shows that some of the videos that
Feldman made were shared with at least three journalists, Jean-François
Cloutier and Jonathan Tremblay of the Journal de Montréal and a Mr. Bialefsky,
whose affiliation was not revealed at trial.
[20]

The Court does not know precisely what videos were communicated to these
journalists and what might have been said about Plaintiffs in them. The most
disparaging videos were produced as exhibit P-25. These are rambling, somewhat

[

Defamation is a civil fault that may be sanctioned by the Courts
under article 1457 C.C.Q. It is a concept that has been well considered in the
jurisprudence. Feldman referred the Court to the judgment of the Supreme Court
of Canada in
Prud’homme v. Prud’homme
:

33

To demonstrate the first element of civil
liability, the existence of injury, the plaintiff must convince the judge that
the impugned remarks were defamatory. The concept of defamation has been
defined in several ways over the years.  Generally speaking, it is held
that defamation [TRANSLATION] “consists in the communication of spoken or
written remarks that cause someone to lose in estimation or consideration, or
that prompt unfavourable or unpleasant feelings toward him or her” (
Radio
Sept‑Îles
,
supra
, at p. 1818).

34

Whether remarks are defamatory is determined by
applying an objective standard (
Hervieux‑Payette v. Société Saint‑Jean‑Baptiste
de Montreal
,
1997 CanLII 8276 (QC CS)
, [1998]
R.J.Q. 131 (Sup. Ct.), at p. 143, reversed on other grounds by
Société
Saint-Jean-Baptiste de Montreal v. Hervieux-Payette
,
2002
CanLII 8266 (QC CA)
, [2002] R.J.Q. 1669 (C.A.)).  In other
words, we must ask whether
an ordinary person would
believe that the remarks made, when viewed as a whole, brought discredit on the
reputation of another person.
On this point, we should note that words
may be defamatory because of the idea they expressly convey, or by the
insinuations that may be inferred from them.  In
Beaudoin v. La
Presse Ltée
,
1997 CanLII 8365 (QC CS)
, [1998] R.J.Q. 204
(Sup. Ct.), at p. 211, Senécal J. provided a good summary of the
approach to be taken in determining whether particular remarks are defamatory
in nature:

[TRANSLATION]  “The form in which the libel is expressed is of little
import; it is the result achieved in the mind of the reader that creates the
delict.”  The defamatory allegation or imputation may be direct, or it may
be indirect, “by simple allusion, insinuation or irony, or be made conditionally,
as an expression of doubt, or hypothetically.”  Often, the allegation or
imputation “is conveyed to the reader by way of a simple insinuation, an
interrogative sentence, a reference to a rumour, mention of information that
has infiltrated the public awareness, juxtaposition of unrelated facts that,
together, take on the appearance of being related”.

The words must also be
interpreted in their context. For instance, “it is not possible to isolate
a passage from a text and complain of it, if the entire text sheds a different
light on that excerpt”.  On the other hand, “it matters little that the
elements of which it is composed are true if the text as a whole conveys a
message that is contrary to reality”.  In fact, truth or reality may be
distorted by half‑truths, selective compilation, omissions, and so on.
“We must consider a newspaper article or radio broadcast as a whole, and the
sentences and words must be interpreted by reference to one another.”

35

However, a person who has made remarks that are
deemed to be defamatory will not necessarily be civilly liable for
them. The plaintiff must further demonstrate that the person who made the
remarks committed a wrongful act.  In
La responsabilité
civile
(5th ed. 1998), at pp. 301‑2, J.-L. Baudouin
and P. Deslauriers point out that in defamation cases, the wrongful act
may derive from two types of conduct, one malicious and the other merely
negligent:

[TRANSLATION]  The
first is an act in which the defendant, knowingly, in bad faith, with intent to
harm, attacks the reputation of the victim and tries to ridicule or humiliate
him or her, expose the victim to the hatred or contempt of the public or a
group. The second results from conduct in which there is no intent to
harm, but in which the defendant has nonetheless interfered with the reputation
of the victim through the defendant’s temerity, negligence, impertinence or
carelessness.  Both kinds of conduct constitute a civil fault and entitle
the victim to reparation, and there is no difference between them in terms of
the right.  In other words, we must refer to the ordinary rules of civil
liability and resolutely abandon the false idea that defamation is only the
result of an act of bad faith where there was intent to harm.

36

Based on the description of these two types of
conduct, we can identify three situations in which a person who made defamatory
remarks could be civilly liable.  The first occurs when a person makes
unpleasant remarks about a third party, knowing them to be false.  Such
remarks could only have been made maliciously, with the intention to harm
another person.  The second situation occurs when a person spreads
unpleasant things about someone else, when he or she should have known them to
be false.  A reasonable person will generally refrain from giving out
unfavourable information about other people if he or she has reason to doubt
the truth of the information.  The third case, which is often forgotten,
is the case of a scandalmonger who makes unfavourable but true statements about
another person without any valid reason for doing so.  (See J. Pineau and M. Ouellette,
Théorie de la
responsabilité civile
(2nd ed. 1980), at pp. 63‑64.)

.,

[6]   To obtain an interlocutory

manifestly defamatory and impossible to justify that an action in defamation
would almost certainly succeed.  Given the value we place on freedom of
expression, particularly in matters of public interest, that guiding principle
has much to recommend it.

[…]

[9]   An interlocutory injunction
should only issue where the evidence shows that the author of the allegedly
defamatory remarks intends to repeat them. Moreover, an interlocutory order
must be restricted to specific statements or comments and cannot apply
generally to all statements of a defamatory character, since such an imprecise
order would constitute an undue restriction on freedom of expression.
[75]

(References omitted)

[
215
]

This is not to say that an individual has a right to make defamatory
statements; he or she does not:

There is no doubt, under our
law, that the Superior Court has jurisdiction to restrain by injunction the
making or publication of defamatory statements which will cause damage or
injury to a person's reputation.  (
Art. 751 C.C.P.
;
Dubois
v.
La
Société Saint-Jean-Baptiste de Montreal

[1983] C.A. 247
;
Scotia
McLeod Inc.
v.
Champagne
,
J.E.
89-1084 (C.S.)
;
Gingras
v.
Entreprises
Télécapitale Ltée
and
Arthur
, C.S. Québec
no. 200‑05‑002850-811,
May 3, 1985
, Bergeron, J.;
Kerr
, Injunctions, 6th edition, 1927,
page 493;
Sharpe
, Injunctions and Specific Performance, 1983,
Toronto Canada Law Book Limited, page 222)
[76]

[
216
]

However, making orders in respect of future and unknown statements
is only appropriate in the clearest of circumstances:

Nor do I believe
we can say what his future comments will be.  Applications for orders
involving prior restraint of future comments or publications, the contents of
which are unknown, must obviously be viewed with the greatest of caution.
(
Woodward
v.
Hutchins
[1977] 2 All E.R. (Eng.
C.A.), see Lord Denning pages 754, 755;
Fraser
v.
Evans

[1969]
1 All E.R. 8
, 12;
Liverpool Household Stores Association
v.
Smith
[1887]
Vol. XXXVII Ch. D. 170, 181)  There are, doubtless, exceptional cases
where it is perfectly clear that the past comments or publications are such
that all future comments or publications are bound to be defamatory and
unjustified as well, and must be restrained.  This is not such a case.
[77]

[
217
]

Considering these principles along with the very broad and general
scope of the requested order, it will not be granted.

[
218
]

Nor will the request that Feldman be required to provide Plaintiffs
with an updated list of the remarks made concerning Plaintiffs. This was
considered and ruled on by way of case management prior to the trial.

5.

The sealing order

[
219
]

Plaintiffs request that exhibits P-10, P-11, P-27 and P-37 in the
present matter remain under seal in the Court record. This would be in keeping
with the following words of the Supreme Court of Canada in
Sherman Estate v.
Donovan
:

[7]

For the reasons that follow, I propose to
recognize an aspect of privacy as an important public interest for the purposes
of the relevant test from
Sierra Club of Canada v. Canada
(Minister of Finance)
,
2002 SCC 41
, [2002]
2 S.C.R. 522. Proceedings in open court can lead to the dissemination
of highly sensitive personal information that would result not just in
discomfort or embarrassment, but in an affront to the affected person’s
dignity. Where this narrower dimension of privacy, rooted in what I see as the
public interest in protecting human dignity, is shown to be at serious risk, an
exception to the open court principle may be justified.
[78]

[
220
]

The purpose of the sealing order would essentially be to protect the
dignity of Andrew and Jonathan and their late mother. This can be an
appropriate reason for the Court to issue a sealing order:

[33]

Personal information disseminated in open court can be
more than a source of discomfort and may result in an affront to a person’s
dignity. Insofar as privacy serves to protect individuals from this affront, it
is an important public interest relevant under
Sierra Club
. Dignity
in this sense is a related but narrower concern than privacy generally; it
transcends the interests of the individual and, like other important public
interests, is a matter that concerns the society at large. A court can make an
exception to the open court principle, notwithstanding the strong presumption
in its favour, if the interest in protecting core aspects of individuals’
personal lives that bear on their dignity is at serious risk by reason of the
dissemination of sufficiently sensitive information. The question is not
whether the information is “personal” to the individual concerned, but whether,
because of its highly sensitive character, its dissemination would occasion an
affront to their dignity that society as a whole has a stake in protecting.

[…]

[35]                          I
hasten to say that applicants for an order making exception to the open court
principle cannot content themselves with an unsubstantiated claim that this
public interest in dignity is compromised any more than they could by an
unsubstantiated claim that their physical integrity is endangered. Under
Sierra
Club
, the applicant must show on the facts of the case that, as an
important interest, this dignity dimension of their privacy is at “serious
risk”. For the purposes of the test for discretionary limits on court openness,
this requires the applicant to show that the information in the court file is
sufficiently sensitive such that it can be said to strike at the biographical
core of the individual and, in the broader circumstances, that there is a
serious risk that, without an exceptional order, the affected individual will
suffer an affront to their dignity.
[79]

[
221
]

In the Court’s view, Plaintiffs have met this burden and the
requested sealing order, greatly diminished from their initial request, is appropriate
save as regards exhibit P-11. Exhibits P-10, P-27 and P-37 are all variations
of Feldman’s Long Form Affidavit. All comprise a somewhat rambling recounting
of the allegations. Although, much of the content of the documents relates to
Lande and not to the Feifers, the Court considers that taken as a whole, the
content might be damaging to Plaintiffs.

[
222
]

Even if the gist of Feldman’s allegations is already in the public
domain, the detail that he exposes in the documents that would be the object of
a sealing order is not, so the order is appropriate.

[
223
]

It is not appropriate as regards exhibit P-11. The resolution is
already in the record of the Commercial Proceedings. Its content is referred to
in detail in those proceedings. Moreover, the defamatory content is also
largely repeated in Plaintiffs’ Originating Application.

6.

Execution Notwithstanding Appeal

[
224
]

Plaintiffs ask for execution notwithstanding appeal under article 661
C.C.P., which reads:

661. Lorsque le fait de porter une
affaire en appel risque de causer un préjudice sérieux ou irréparable à une partie,
le juge peut, sur demande, ordonner l’exécution provisoire, même partielle; il
peut aussi subordonner l’exécution provisoire à la constitution d’une caution.

Si l’exécution provisoire n’est pas
ordonnée par le jugement lui-même, elle ne peut plus l’être qu’en appel, avec
ou sans caution. Un juge de la Cour d’appel peut aussi la suspendre ou la lever
lorsqu’elle a été ordonnée, ou encore assujettir la partie qui en a été
dispensée par le tribunal de première instance à fournir un cautionnement.

[
225
]

Plaintiffs argue that the record offers a demonstration that without
an order under article 661 C.C.P., Feldman will simply go to appeal and will
continue to defame them.

[
226
]

The Court will not issue the requested order. It is up to Plaintiffs
to demonstrate why it would be necessary.
[80]

They have not done so. Contrary to their argument, there is no evidence that
Feldman continues to defame them or intends to do so.
